entries.english: Phonetic System, Ogaden/Darod Dialect Note, Swahili Coast Terms, Currency (Rubiad/Rubi) & Cultural Lexicon in de Larajasse (1897)
entries.translation: Phonetic & Orthographic System (Preface pp. v–xiii): Cerebral d (tongue curved against front of palate, sounding like rd in 'hard'), strong chest aspirate h (Arabic ح), guttural h (representing Arabic غ ق خ, two-thirds from ق), pharyngealized vowels ‘a/a‘, ‘e/e‘, ‘i/i‘, ‘o/o‘, ‘u/u‘ (Arabic ع), hollow diphthong ow, interchangeable k/g and t/d, interdental y in maya ('no', pronounced matha), and absence of p, v, z (replaced by b, f/b, s) • Swahili & Social Status Terms (pp. 123, 127, 242, 266): sawaheli / sawahili,—gi (m.n., Swahili coast person / slave, alongside adon,—ki [m.] / adon,—ti [f.] and bida/bidai,—ihi [m.] / bidad,—di [f.]); singal,—ki (m.n., client who comes under the protection of a powerful patron, p. 127); serkal,—ki (government/authority, p. 123) • Ogaden, Dulbanteh & Darod Dialect Note (Supplement p. 293): wa debai / wa i debai (verbal locution specifically noted as used in the Ogaden and by the Dulbanteh and Darod, vs. standard sino / sinaiso, p. 127) • Currency & Fractions (pp. 118, 293): rubiad,—di (f.n., pl. rubabi; contracted in counting to rubod instead of rubiadod = 1 rupee), rubi (m.n. = 1 shilling / 8 annas, half-rupee), sarrif,—ki (money-changing: 'rubiadda i sarrif', p. 123), dalol,—ki (m.n., numeral fraction one-third, p. 293) • Pastoral, Medical & Domestic Customs (pp. 26, 123, 266, 293): dabsi / dabsin,—ti (separating a young camel from its mother by day or exchanging two sucklings, p. 26); sarsar,—ki (medicinal skin-incision / scarification of sick or pot-bellied children, p. 123); burambur (women's song, p. 293) vs. gabai / hes (song/poetry, gabaya,—ihi singer, p. 266); dardar,—ki (the 3 hearth-stones supporting the cooking pot, p. 293); sibrar,—ki (leathern water-bag, p. 127); 'sadehda dalahod bad igaga furaisantahai' (triple-divorce oath formula under dalah, p. 293)
entries.pronunciation: sah-wah-heh-lee • roo-bee-ahd (pl. roo-bah-bee, count. roo-bohd) / roo-bee • see-ngahl • boo-rahm-boor • dahr-dahr
